newsitem.title: DENMARK: SOCCER-DANES WREST VICTORY FROM TOUGH BOSNIANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DANES WREST VICTORY FROM TOUGH BOSNIANS.

text.p: Denmark beat Bosnia 2-0 in their World Cup qualifier on Sunday to consolidate their position at the top of group one.
They head the group with 13 points from five games. Greece are second with 10 points after six games.
"It was a difficult match, and we are very, very lucky that we won. We could easily have lost 1-0. The Bosnians played high-quality football," Danish trainer Bo Johannsen said.
For much of the match the biggest stars were the goalkeepers. Despite tight Bosnian marking the Danes created the most chances in the first half but failed to get the ball past Mirsad Dedic.
The second half opened with the Bosnians exploiting a gap in the Danish defence to get in a clear shot, but Peter Schmeichel denied them.

In the 61st minute the Danes drew first blood with a header by Marc Rieper off a pass from Jan Heintze, who picked up the ball just outside the penalty box from a corner kick delivered by Brian Laudrup.
The Bosnians fought back hard after Rieper's goal but Schmeichel held them at bay and in the final minute of injury time substitute Miklos Molnar crowned the Danish victory with a second goal.
Molnar, Danish-born of Hungarian descent, got his chance when a Bosnian defender trying to get the ball away from the goalmouth accidently delivered it at his feet.
Though he heads the Danish scoring table with 25 goals this season for his club Lyngby, it was Molnar's first international goal.
"Denmark were very dangerous after free kicks and corners," Bosnian trainer Fuad Muzurovic acknowledged, adding that he thought his side played well despite injury problems.
